title: Severity-Controlled Prediction Sets for Medication Recommendation
claim: Standard metrics score different prediction sets as equivalent; our severity-aware measure separates close mismatches from distant ones.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right with arrows, equal-metric vs severity-aware contrast
description: Three panels read left to right, joined by thick black arrows. The left panel has a dashed blue rounded box titled 'Many Plausible Prediction Sets for Drug Recommendation'. It lists Sets A–E, each a short list of drug names such as Lisinopril, Warfarin and Metformin. The middle panel, 'Traditional Measures Treat Errors Equally', is a gray-headed rounded card showing the ground truth [Metformin, Lisinopril]. Below it, Set 1 [Metformin, Enalapril] and Set 2 [Metformin, Warfarin] each carry a light-blue 'Recall=1/2' tag, with an equals sign between them. The right panel, 'CSC Distinguishes Mismatch Severity', repeats the ground truth. Set 1 gets a green 'Low Severity' tag and a check mark. Set 2 gets a red 'High severity' tag and an X. The eye goes first to the colored tags and the check and cross.
caption: Motivation for Conformal Severity Control (CSC). Prediction sets can achieve the same recall while differing substantially in ATC mismatch severity. CSC selects a score threshold on calibration data so that the expected severity stays below a user-specified tolerance.
abstract: Medication recommendation is a multi-label prediction task. However, existing prediction-set evaluation and calibration methods rely mainly on exact-overlap metrics and therefore treat all missed medications as equally severe, overlooking how closely the prediction set matches them within the medication hierarchy. To address this, we introduce Conformal Severity Control (CSC), a post-hoc framework for calibrating medication prediction sets under hierarchy-aware mismatch severity. CSC uses the Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical (ATC) hierarchy to quantify mismatch severity and controls patient-level severity without retraining the predictor, supporting both average severity and upper-quantile severity for the highest-severity mismatches. Experiments on MIMIC-IV show that CSC tracks user-specified severity tolerances and shifts prediction sets away from distant mismatches toward exact or close matches.
